title.narrative: Supporting Conflict Affected IDPs in Afar region, Ethiopia

description.narrative: APDA will implement the proposed interventions in consultation and coordination with DPFSPCO, the shelter cluster group and the Afar Emergency Coordination Committee under the leadership of OCHA. The target beneficiaries of food and shelter NFI will be IDPs who are temporarily hosted by the local community. APDA will refer cluster standards and use its existing community structures and partnership with key stakeholders in beneficiary selection process. Thus, the proposed project will target the most vulnerable HHs who constitute affected children, girls, women, female headed HHs, and households with special needs (PSN) including PWD, PLW, elders, and person chronically ill people who have been affected by the conflict.

The humanitarian context in Afar region has drastically deteriorated since the spillover of the conflict in Tigray in July 2021. Prior to this conflict, the region had already significant humanitarian needs due to drought, conflict, and disease outbreaks as per the 2021 Humanitarian Response Plan Mid-Year Review. Over the past few weeks, while the border regions of Tigray and Amhara have been relatively calm, heavy clashes were reported in Afar Region (incl. by UNOCHA - ). This recent conflict has had a heavy toll on affected communities. Several hundreds of thousands of people in Afar region were uprooted from their homes in search of safety and assistance. The UNOCHA situation reports1-2 indicate that 200.000 people have been displaced due to the recent fighting, and new IDPs are coming in every day as fighting continues. The vast majority of the displaced have been living with the host community, while others are sheltered in IDP sites, including in schools with minimal assistance. According to the Afar regional authorities, many IDPs are scattered in remote areas with little or no access to critical items such as food and water. This is confirmed by an assessment conducted by local partner APDA. Serious malnutrition rates are already reported.

is to provide emergency supports for conflict affected IDPs in Afar region, Ethiopia. The proposed intervention aims to reach 2,130 Households (HHs) (10,650 individuals) in Sifera and Magaale Woreda of Afar region through the distribution of Food for 880 HHs and Shelter NFIs for 1,250 HHs.

title.narrative: The Humanitarian Response was Timely

description.narrative:
SPHERE: Communities and people affected by crisis, including the most vulnerable groups, consider that the timing of the assistance and protection they receive is adequate. DRA: timely depends on the nature of the acute crisis (slow versus sudden onset). If it is an acute sudden onset crisis a response is considered timely if we decide to respond within 48 hours and if we initiate the response within 72 hours. If it is a slow onset crisis, it is timely if we initiate the response in 3 weeks after we decide that the crisis meets the criteria of an acute crisis.
The applicable definition depends on the type of crisis (protracted versus acute). The SPHERE definition should be used in more protracted crisis where there is (more) time to conduct assessments and measure satisfaction of the response in the eyes of people affected. The DRA definition should be used for acute crises, where it is more important to initiate the response as soon as possible and look at our own processes.

title.narrative: Climate Resilience
The project integrates climate risks in programming

description.narrative: The integration of climate risks in programming includes an undertaking of concrete actions to reduce and/or mitigate risks related to climate change impact and disaster risks ( for example droughts, erosion, salinization, flooding, etc.) The projects we refer to could be on the themes of health education, justice, security, disaster management, finance and livelihoods.
